about: How-to help for the NetSentinel website, written from the shipped UI and API. Every entry lists anchors: exact strings it quotes and the file they come from. tests/test_help_kb.py fails if an anchor disappears, so a renamed button or changed limit cannot leave this text stale silently.

entries.title: Creating an account and signing in
entries.where: The sign-in page (/auth) - every page sends you there when you are not signed in
entries.summary: NetSentinel has no anonymous mode: every page needs an account. The sign-in page has a "Sign up" link for a new account and a "Sign in" link back.
steps: On the sign-in page, click "Sign up".
Enter your Full Name and Email Address. Phone Number and Date of Birth are optional.
Choose a password that meets at least three of the checks shown under it: At least 8 characters, an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a number, a special character.
Type it again in Confirm Password, tick the Privacy Policy & Terms of Service box, and create the account.
Open the confirmation email and click its link, then sign in with your email and password.
A new account with no machines yet is taken to the Getting Started page after signing in.

problems.symptom: "Please confirm your email first" when signing in
fixes: Open the confirmation email NetSentinel sent and click its link, then sign in again.
Check your spam folder if it is not in your inbox.

problems.symptom: "Invalid email or password"
fixes: Check the email address for typos and try the password again.
Use "Forgot password?" under the password box to set a new one.

problems.symptom: "An account with this email already exists"
fixes: Click "Sign in" and sign in with that email instead, or reset its password with "Forgot password?".

problems.symptom: "Password is too weak"
fixes: Meet at least three of the strength checks listed under the password field.

problems.symptom: "Too many attempts right now"
fixes: Wait a little while, then try again.

anchors.text: Account created! Check your email for a confirmation link, then sign in.
Password is too weak. Please meet at least 3 strength criteria.

entries.title: Resetting a forgotten password
entries.summary: Use "Forgot password?" on the sign-in page to get a reset link by email, then choose a new password.
steps: On the sign-in page, click "Forgot password?" under the password box.
Enter your email address and click "Send reset link".
Open the email and click the link. It opens "Set a New Password".
Enter a new password of at least 8 characters twice and save it. You are then signed in.

problems.symptom: No reset email arrives
fixes: Check your spam folder.
Make sure you typed the email address the account was created with. For privacy the page says the same thing whether or not an account exists.

problems.symptom: "This reset link has expired or was already used"
fixes: Request a new link with "Forgot password?" and use the newest email.

anchors.text: This reset link has expired or was already used. Request a new one.
If an account exists for that email, a reset link is on its way.

entries.title: Signing out, and using several devices
entries.summary: Your data belongs to your account, not to a browser, so you can sign in from more than one computer or browser and see the same devices and history. "Sign Out" at the bottom of the sidebar ends the session and returns you to the sign-in page.
steps: To sign out, click "Sign Out" at the bottom of the sidebar.
To use another computer or browser, sign in there with the same email and password.

problems.symptom: "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."
fixes: Your session expired or was signed out elsewhere. Sign in again; your devices and history are kept on your account.

problems.symptom: Using a shared computer
fixes: Click "Sign Out" when you finish, so the next person cannot use your session.

anchors.text: Your session has ended. Please sign in again.

entries.title: Adding a machine to monitor (installing the agent)
entries.summary: Adding a device is how you add any machine - any target - you want NetSentinel to monitor. Each machine you want to monitor runs the NetSentinel agent, a single downloadable file with nothing else to install. You link it to your account with a short code from the website. There is no install command to paste: you download the file, run it, and type the code.
steps: Open Devices in the sidebar and click "Add a device".
Choose the operating system of the machine you are adding - Windows (Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit) or Linux (x86-64, most distributions, such as Ubuntu or Debian) - not the one you are reading this on.
Click the download button. If you downloaded it on a different computer, copy the file to the machine you are adding; it contains no account details, so copying it is safe.
On that machine, run the file. On Windows, double-click it. It asks for an enrolment code.
On the website, continue to the step "Run it, and type in this code" and type the 8-character code it shows into the agent.
Leave the wizard open: it notices the machine checking in by itself and moves to Done. The machine then appears on the Devices page, and telemetry arrives every minute.

problems.symptom: "This code has expired."
fixes: A code works once and expires after 15 minutes. Click "New code" in the wizard and type the new one.

problems.symptom: The agent says "That code was not accepted."
fixes: Check you typed all 8 characters. Dashes, spaces and lower case are fine.
If the code has expired or was already used, click "New code" in the wizard.

problems.symptom: Two machines show up as one device
fixes: Each machine registers under its own hostname. Two machines with the same hostname are treated as one device, so give them distinct names.

problems.symptom: Running it from a terminal instead of double-clicking
fixes: On Windows: .\netsentinel-agent-windows.exe --enroll
On Linux: chmod +x netsentinel-agent-linux && ./netsentinel-agent-linux --enroll

Note that --enroll links and registers the machine and then exits. Start reporting afterwards with --start: .
etsentinel-agent-windows.exe --start on Windows, ./netsentinel-agent-linux --start on Linux.

anchors.text: Run it, and type in this code
two machines sharing a hostname are treated as one device
It is on your Devices page now. Telemetry arrives every minute.

entries.title: "Waiting for the machine to check in" - what it means
entries.where: Devices -> "Add a device", the last step
entries.summary: After you type the code into the agent, the wizard waits for that machine to register with your account. It usually takes a few seconds, and the wizard updates on its own - there is nothing to click.
steps: Keep the wizard open on the website after typing the code into the agent.
When the machine registers, the wizard moves to Done and the machine is listed on the Devices page.

problems.symptom: It keeps waiting and nothing appears
fixes: Look at the agent's window on that machine for a message - it says if the code was rejected or the server could not be reached.
Check that the code has not expired; if it has, click "New code" and enter the new one.
Make sure that machine can reach the internet: a firewall blocking outbound HTTPS stops the agent from registering.
On that machine, run the agent with --status to see whether it is linked and registered.

anchors.text: Waiting for the machine to check in
Check the agent window for a message, and that the code has

entries.title: My device shows OFFLINE (the agent stopped reporting)
entries.summary: OFFLINE means NetSentinel has had no report from that machine's agent for more than 3 minutes (it reports every minute). The machine itself may be fine - usually the agent program is no longer running on it.
steps: Start the agent again on that machine. If you use the downloaded file, double-click it, or run it with --start from a terminal: .\netsentinel-agent-windows.exe --start on Windows, ./netsentinel-agent-linux --start on Linux.
If you installed from source on the Getting Started page, run python agent/agent.py --start in that folder with its virtual environment active.
The device returns to ONLINE with its next report, within about a minute.

problems.symptom: It goes OFFLINE a few minutes after I added it
fixes: If you linked it from a terminal with --enroll, that command registers the machine and then exits. Run the agent with --start to keep it reporting.

problems.symptom: It goes OFFLINE whenever the machine restarts or I close the window
fixes: The agent only reports while it is running. With the downloaded file, start it again after a restart.

With the source install, run the auto-start installer from the Getting Started page once: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File agent\install_autostart.ps1 on Windows, or bash agent/install_autostart.sh on Linux/macOS. It starts the agent at login and restarts it if it stops.

problems.symptom: The agent is running but the device stays OFFLINE
fixes: Check that the machine can reach the internet and that no firewall blocks outbound HTTPS.
Run the agent with --status to confirm it is linked to your account.

anchors.text: The machine itself may be fine

entries.title: Installing the agent from source, and the agent token (Getting Started page)
entries.where: Sidebar -> Getting Started (shown until your first machine is registered)
entries.summary: The Getting Started page shows a second way to run the agent: from the source code with Python, configured with a personal agent token in a .env file. Most people should use "Add a device" instead, which needs no Python and no token.
steps: Get the agent (needs git and Python 3.10+): git clone https://github.com/SiddharthaChathra/NetSentinal, then cd NetSentinal.
Create and activate a virtual environment. Linux / macOS: python3 -m venv .venv then source .venv/bin/activate. Windows (PowerShell): python -m venv .venv then .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1.
Install the agent's dependencies: pip install -r agent/requirements.txt
Create a file named .env in the NetSentinal folder with the two lines the page shows: API_BASE_URL and your AGENT_TOKEN.
Register and start: python agent/agent.py --register, then python agent/agent.py --start.
Optionally run the auto-start installer the page shows, so the agent starts at login.

problems.symptom: "externally-managed-environment" when running pip install
fixes: Create and activate the virtual environment first, as the page shows. On Ubuntu, if creating it fails, install python3-venv.

problems.symptom: The agent says the server rejected the agent token (401)
fixes: Copy the current AGENT_TOKEN line from the Getting Started page into .env. Tokens change when someone clicks "Generate new token".

problems.symptom: I clicked "Generate new token"
fixes: Every agent using the old token stops reporting until its .env is updated with the new one.

anchors.text: Create a file named .env in the NetSentinal folder
Any agent using the old token will stop reporting until updated.
The server rejected the agent token (401).

entries.title: Removing a device
entries.summary: "Remove" on a device's card deletes the device and all of its telemetry from your account.
steps: Open Devices and find the device's card.
Click "Remove" at the bottom of the card and confirm.

problems.symptom: The device comes back after I remove it
fixes: Its agent is still running and registers it again. Stop the agent on that machine first.

anchors.text: and all of its telemetry? If its agent is still running, stop it or re-register it afterwards.

entries.title: Understanding the Health Score
entries.summary: The Health Score on the Overview page is a 0-100 summary of the most recent diagnostic run. It starts at 100 and loses points for each problem found.
steps: Gateway unreachable and nothing beyond it reachable: -40. A gateway that only ignores ping while traffic still flows costs 3.
Internet unreachable: -30.
Every DNS lookup failing: -15. Every TCP service check failing: -15.
Packet loss: minus the loss percentage, up to -20.
Latency above 100 ms: -5, or -10 above 300 ms.
The status reads HEALTHY at 90 or more with no warnings, HEALTHY (WITH WARNINGS) from 80, WARNING from 60, and CRITICAL below 60.

problems.symptom: The score shows a dash
fixes: No diagnostic has run yet. Click "Run Diagnostic" on the Overview page.

problems.symptom: The score does not describe my own computer
fixes: "Run Diagnostic" on the Overview page runs from the NetSentinel server, not from your computer. To measure your own machines, add them with "Add a device".

entries.title: The Overview page: Run Diagnostic and Guided Troubleshooting
entries.summary: The Overview shows the Health Score, Monitored Devices, Active Incidents and Average Latency. "Run Diagnostic" runs a full check from the NetSentinel server; the menu beside it can instead run a demo scenario.
steps: Click "Run Diagnostic" to run a scan. Leave the menu on "Normal Scan (Real Network)" for a real check, or pick a demo (DNS Failure, Gateway Failure, TCP Failure, High Latency, Packet Loss) to see how a problem is reported.

Under Guided Troubleshooting, click "Why is my network slow?" for an analysis built from measured history. It names the machine it measured, compares latency with that machine's baseline, and says when there is not enough data yet.

problems.symptom: It says it measured the NetSentinel server, not my network
fixes: The hosted scan runs on the NetSentinel server. Add your own machine with "Add a device" so the analysis can use it.

problems.symptom: "Awaiting Network Data" or "Run a diagnostic to see latency"
fixes: No diagnostic has run yet. Click "Run Diagnostic", or add a device so its agent starts reporting.

anchors.text: Measured by the NetSentinel server on its own network, not yours.

entries.title: Backup Readiness, and what NFS, SMB, iSCSI and Replication readiness mean
entries.where: Sidebar -> Backup Readiness (targets are tagged on the Devices page)
entries.summary: Backup Readiness answers: if a backup job started against this machine now, would it work and finish inside your SLA window? It scores each device you have tagged as a backup target from 0 to 100.
steps: On the Devices page, turn on the "Backup Target" switch on the machine that receives backups, then choose the protocols it serves: NFS, SMB, iSCSI or Replication. Only the chosen ones are checked.
Open Backup Readiness. Enter your job's size in Dataset (GB) and your window in SLA (Hrs).

Readiness of a protocol means its port is open on that machine: NFS is port 2049, SMB is port 445, iSCSI is port 3260, and Replication is port 10000 unless your deployment configures another. The agent checks these on the machine itself.

Each target starts at 100: unreachable -50, DNS not resolving -25, some required ports closed -22 (all closed -30), and an estimated transfer that is tight against the SLA -18 or misses it -35. 85 or more is ready, 55 to 84 at-risk, below 55 not-ready.
The transfer-time estimate is directional: it is derived from measured latency and packet loss and an assumed link speed, not from a bandwidth test.
The menu at the top can run a demo scenario (DNS Flap, Port Blocked, Throughput Drop) instead of Live Data.

problems.symptom: "No backup targets configured"
fixes: Tag a device as a backup target on the Devices page with the "Backup Target" switch.

problems.symptom: A protocol shows as closed
fixes: The backup service is not listening on that port on the machine, or a firewall on it blocks the port. Start the service, or allow the port.
If the machine does not serve that protocol, untick it under the device's protocols so it is not scored.

problems.symptom: "Not scanned (host unreachable)"
fixes: The target could not be reached at all, so its ports could not be checked. Check that the machine is on and its agent is running.

entries.title: Reading the diagnostics feed
entries.where: Backup Readiness page, below the targets
entries.summary: The diagnostics feed lists each problem the rule engine found on your backup targets: which target, how severe (critical, warning or info), what it found, and a Recommendation saying what to check.
steps: Read the target name and severity first, then the message, then the Recommendation underneath it.
"No active issues" means every monitored target passed its checks.

entries.title: Incidents: acknowledging, resolving, and write-ups
entries.summary: An incident is a problem NetSentinel detected on one of your devices. The Incidents page lists them with filters (All, Open, Critical, Resolved); click one to see its likely cause, evidence and recommended checks.
steps: Click an incident to expand it.
On an open incident, click "Acknowledge" to mark it seen, or "Resolve" to close it.
"Write up for a ticket" writes a plain-English summary of the incident, and "KB article" turns it into a short knowledge-base article.

problems.symptom: An incident closed by itself
fixes: Packet loss, latency, DNS and gateway incidents are closed automatically once the agent's reports show the problem has stopped.

problems.symptom: There are no incidents
fixes: Nothing has been detected. Incidents only appear when a device's agent reports a problem.

entries.title: History and baselines
entries.summary: History charts Health Score, latency and packet loss over a chosen range (1h, 6h, 24h, 7d or 30d), with a Baseline Summary of average, median, 95th percentile and standard deviation.
steps: Open History and pick a range at the top.
Read the Baseline Summary for what is normal for your network.

problems.symptom: "No History Available"
fixes: Nothing has been recorded in that range yet. Run a diagnostic from the Overview page, or add a device so its agent starts reporting.

entries.title: The Topology page
entries.summary: Topology draws the path your machines take to the internet: Internet Gateway, then Default Gateway, then each of your registered devices. It is a logical view of the devices on your account - it does not scan or discover other devices on your network.
steps: Open Topology to see each registered device and whether its gateway and internet were reachable in its latest report.
A machine only appears here after you add it with "Add a device".

problems.symptom: A device on my network is missing from the map
fixes: NetSentinel does not auto-discover devices. Install the agent on it with "Add a device".

anchors.text: Network topology is logical (registered devices), not auto-discovered

entries.title: Downloading a report
entries.summary: The Reports page builds a network health report assembled by the server, so its numbers match the dashboard. Choose JSON Export, Markdown Export or PDF Report, then click "Download Report".
steps: Open Reports and choose a format under Export Options.

Click "Download Report". The PDF is the full engineer's report: executive summary, layer-by-layer evidence, device telemetry, trend graphs, backup readiness with the SLA arithmetic, and a methodology appendix.

problems.symptom: "Nothing to report yet"
fixes: Run a diagnostic from the Overview page, or add a device first.

entries.title: The welcome tour
entries.where: Shown automatically after your first sign-in
entries.summary: A short welcome tour runs once per account, after your first successful sign-in. It is remembered on your account rather than in the browser, so it does not repeat on another computer.
steps: There is currently no button on the website to replay the tour.

entries.title: Nothing is showing up (empty pages)
entries.summary: Most empty pages mean no machine on your account is reporting yet. NetSentinel only shows data that it has actually measured.
steps: Check Devices. If it lists no machines, add one with "Add a device" - Overview, History, Topology and Incidents fill in once its agent reports.
If your devices show OFFLINE, their agents have stopped reporting; start them again (see "My device shows OFFLINE").
If a banner says "Waking up the server, this can take up to a minute", wait - the data loads once the server is up.
Backup Readiness stays empty until you tag a device as a backup target.

anchors.text: Waking up the server, this can take up to a minute.

entries.title: "Connecting to NetSentinel" and "Waking up the server"
entries.where: Banner at the top of the page
entries.summary: The NetSentinel server sleeps when nobody has used it for a while and takes up to a minute to wake. The banner shows while it starts; the page loads by itself once it is up.
steps: Wait for the banner to clear - it keeps retrying on its own.
If it says "We couldn't reach the NetSentinel service", it may be restarting. It keeps trying; check your own internet connection if it lasts more than a few minutes.

anchors.text: We couldn't reach the NetSentinel service. It may be restarting

entries.title: Using the assistant (Ask NetSentinel)
entries.where: The chat button at the bottom right, and Sidebar -> Assistant
entries.summary: Ask NetSentinel answers questions about your own diagnostic findings and about how to use this website. It only uses your account's recorded findings and this help, and says so when they do not cover a question. The Assistant page also has a daily or weekly digest and 30-day trends per device.
steps: Open the chat with the round button at the bottom right, or open Assistant in the sidebar.
Ask about a device by name, a kind of problem (DNS, latency, packet loss, gateway), a time range (today, this week), or how to do something on the website.

problems.symptom: "The assistant is temporarily unavailable"
fixes: The AI service could not be reached. Your diagnostic data is unaffected; try again shortly.

anchors.text: The assistant is temporarily unavailable. Your diagnostic data is unaffected.
